featured_reviews.name: Tanaya More
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I could give a minus, I totally would. Our entire experience was nothing short of a nightmare.

We had a 10:30 PM appointment with Dr. Virendra Yadav and made sure to arrive on time. However, the doctor only showed up at 12:15 AM. Waiting nearly two hours late at night without any proper communication or explanation is simply unacceptable.

Around 11:30 PM, while we were still waiting and the doctor hadn’t arrived, the reception staff insisted that we pay the consultation advance immediately. We calmly said we would pay once the doctor came, because at that point there was no clarity on whether he would even show up. We were then told that if we paid later, we would be charged emergency consultation fees. It felt unfair and unnecessarily pressurizing.

Things became even more upsetting when my father started feeling severe acidity due to the long wait. The hospital has an in-house pharmacy, so he requested a simple Digene tablet and was ready to pay for it. The pharmacist refused and told him, “Doctor se prescription leke aao ya phir bahar jaao main road pe waha chemist hoga.” This was between 12:00–12:30 AM. Being asked to step out onto the main road at midnight for basic relief medication was shocking and showed a complete lack of empathy.

The receptionist’s behavior throughout was extremely rude and dismissive. In a hospital, patients are already stressed and vulnerable. The least one expects is basic courtesy and compassion which was clearly missing.

Overall, it was a deeply distressing experience. Hospitals are supposed to provide care and reassurance. Unfortunately, we felt neither cared for nor respected.

Update after the Hospital’s response:

Thank you for your response, but unfortunately it does not address the core issues we faced that night.

While delays due to emergencies can happen in healthcare, what was unacceptable was the complete lack of communication. Patients were simply left waiting for nearly two hours late at night without any update about the doctor’s arrival. Basic transparency would have avoided much of the frustration.

Regarding the advance payment, the concern was not about the billing protocol itself, but the manner in which it was handled. Asking patients to pay in advance when the doctor had not even arrived yet, and then telling us that paying later would lead to “emergency charges” was extremely unreasonable. If the doctor had arrived at the scheduled time, our consultation would have been completed well before midnight. It is unfair to suggest emergency charges when the delay was entirely on the hospital’s side and not the patient’s.

Your explanation about prescription requirements at the pharmacy is also not convincing in this situation. Digene is an over-the-counter antacid, not a restricted medication. My father was clearly uncomfortable due to acidity after waiting late into the night, yet instead of showing basic empathy or offering assistance, he was told to go out to the main road to find a chemist at 12-12:30 am.That response showed a serious lack of patient care.

Another concerning issue was during the consultation itself. When the doctor finally arrived, the door of the consultation room was not even closed, and conversations between the doctor and patient could easily be heard from outside. Patient-doctor privacy is a basic expectation in any medical setting, and this lack of confidentiality was highly unprofessional.

Most importantly, the attitude of the reception staff was extremely rude and dismissive throughout the entire interaction. This was not simply a communication gap, it was a matter of basic courtesy and empathy, which were clearly missing.

While I acknowledge your apology, the experience that night reflected serious gaps in patient care, communication, and professionalism. I hope this feedback leads to meaningful corrective action, so that other patients and families are not put through a similar experience in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Vijay Saw
featured_reviews.review_text:
💔 I lost a close friend recently due to medical negligence. Here’s what happened, and I hope sharing this will help others be more aware.

My friend had a small fracture in his leg. He decided to visit a private hospital called Mangal Murti for faster service.
The doctor suggested giving anesthesia before applying a plaster cast. This was supposed to be a simple procedure, taking about 45 minutes.
During the procedure, the first dose of anesthesia didn’t work, so the doctor gave another dose.
After the procedure, his pulse was not responding. The medical team panicked and gave an anti-anesthesia shot, but nothing worked.
They told the family to take him to a government hospital urgently. The family was shocked — he had walked into the hospital himself, riding his scooter. How could his pulse suddenly stop?
The family rushed him to multiple hospitals. The reports showed severe brain and kidney damage. Despite moving him to a better facility and spending four days in intensive care, he didn’t recover.
In the end, the doctors admitted their mistake and tried to settle it with money. The police, who were practically guarding the hospital, sided with the doctor who did the operation, offering protection to the hospital.
🙏 I’m not asking for sympathy, but I want to raise awareness. Please avoid Mangal Murti hospital, no matter what the situation is. After this incident, I found out that they literally sell body parts.

This is a reminder to always ask questions and be vigilant during medical treatments, even for routine procedures. My friend’s life was lost due to negligence, and I don’t want this to happen to anyone else.

If you can’t provide quality care, don’t risk someone’s life for the sake of money

featured_reviews.name: Ritesh Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience. Writing after a week from discharge.
++ Visited this hospital for first time in my life.

Location: 5minutes away from Borivali W railway station. Landmark: Diamond Talkies, Lokmanya Tilak / LT Road. From LT Road, there is a small lane - 1 car can pass at a time next to Benzer readmade clothes shop. Go inside the small lane. Left hand side you will see Purohit hospital and right hand side you will see residential building. Take left lane to reach hospital.

++ Had been hospitalized due to COVID for 10days.
++ Dedicated COVID center.
++ Patients are NOT allowed to roam inside and outside hospital premise.
++ Families are NOT allowed to visit dedicated COVID center room area. Only reception area is allowed.
++ Ground floor and first floor with beds.
++ Great services by nurses viz.; experienced nurses, prompt room service when alarmed using WiFi device kept next to patient beds, timely reminder and feed of medicines, routinely check-up from morning till night 10pm, nurse shifts changes 3 times a day (24 hours).
++ Packaged breakfast in morning with tea/coffee, Packaged lunch, Packaged breakfast in evening with tea / coffee and packaged Dinner given to COVID patients. Being a foodie, the packaged food was of Quality, quantity, protein, nutritious and it was delicious. Believe me. Everyday it taste great with variety of menu's.
++ Have heard, foods from hotel can be ordered and delivered to patient by clerks. I never need to avail that service since packaged food was better.
++ Warm water on request given to patients by clerks.
++ Turmeric Milk given to patients at night.
++ Daily cleaning of rooms by clerks 2 - 3 times a day.
++ Beds are normal. Please do not expect 3 star or 5 star category beds here. Nice beds that gives your back proper rest and it does not pain. i don't have back-pains / slip-dic disease so point to be noted for patients with back-pain.
++ Junior doctor visits twice a day 9am and 7pm answers queries and guides.
++ Main Doctor (MD  Physician) visits twice a day 11:30am and 8:30pm at patient beds and answers queries and guides.
++ For washing clothes, you can ask for cleaner who washes clothes of patients on requests. This is not billed to hospital. patient and cleaner to manage internally and is charged lumsum.
++ Most important, oxygen cylinders are available and given to patients on MD doctor's advice and consultation. Daily morning oxygen cylinders are delivered / exchanged at hospital premises.
++ Remdisiver injections are given to COVID patients on MD doctor advice and on time.
++ During my tenure, the hospital was not fully consumed / less patients 10 patients approx.
++ Total 3 toilets available in hospital. During my tenure, i did not face difficulties and was able to manage myself. Toilets are cleaned twice - thrice a day. there is availability of hot water for bathing.
++ Clean premise. Silent environment. Good ventilation.
++ Small hospital but i appreciate the way they treated to ME!
++ Not that expensive.
++ Treatment was done well.
